text:
maria: Quick forum — product wants a clear prioritization for routing/isolation work next 6mo. Customers asking for SLA guarantees + a "no-surprises" migration path. Can we align on what to scope for Q2?

sam: We should categorize asks by impact: Revenue (customers blocked), Risk (compliance/data residency), Cost (ops/egress), and Complexity (infra + migration).

jon: +1. I'd add a quick scoring rubric so PM can defend ask prioritization to GTM. Something like: revenue_score 1-5, unblock_score 1-5, infra_risk 1-5.

tara: Specific asks from enterprise pilots: 1) pinned-region routing for data residency 2) tenant CPU/GPU quotas + soft eviction 3) documented fallback order with quality delta metrics.

maria: Proposal: for Q2 we do a "Minimum Viable Isolation" (MVI) that covers pinned-region + simple quota gating + audit logs. Save full soft eviction + canary cutover tooling for Q3. Objections?

sam: Concern: pinned-region without fallback policies will cause availability regressions for tenants during outages. We need a playable fallback default. Maybe 'local-prefer, cross-region-degrade' with opt-out.

jon: Also need clear SLOs to ship with MVI. Suggest: 95p tail latency delta <250ms for warm requests when using regional routing; failover path documented with RTO goals.

tara: Customers are asking for an SLA number not just delta. Can we commit to an availability SLA for hosted tenants in a pinned region? That triggers legal/finance discussions.

maria: For MVI, let's avoid hard SLA commitments. Instead offer "best-effort" with clear caveats and a roadmap to SLA in Dedicated/Private. We'll add an enterprise offering path to buy an SLA-backed Dedicated pool.

sam: That maps cleanly. Also call out cost: cross-region failover increases egress and may incur extra token cost. We need a billing flag or quota to prevent surprise invoices.

jon: Acceptance tests: synthetic tail-latency, cross-region correctness tests, and a small-scale canary to validate fallback quality (use a holdout prompt set).

tara: UX asks: a tenant-level toggle for routing behavior (auto-fallback vs strict-residency) + an action "promote to dedicated" that signals sales to start the contract flow. Console mocks will be ready tomorrow.

ops-bot: infra-bot: noted. Open ticket INFRA-2217 created to track gating for quota enforcement and telemetry.

maria: Dependencies: KMS for region-bound encryption, routing policy engine updates (policy precedence), and billing flags. Who owns KMS? @sam?

sam: I can take KMS integration but need crypto/security pairing. Also need a short design doc on key rotation implications for KV cache invalidation.

jon: For rollout plan, suggest three phases: 1) opt-in pilot (limited tenants) 2) opt-out default with monitoring 3) GA with org-level controls. Each phase has explicit acceptance gates.

tara: Can we get a prioritization matrix by EOD Fri? PM wants to show it in next GTM sync. I'll own the PM side if you folks provide the scoring inputs.

maria: Agree. I'll draft the scoring guidance: revenue weight 0.4, risk 0.3, cost 0.2, complexity -0.1. Send your scores by Thu so I can compile.

sam: I'll add estimated engineering effort (T-shirt sizing) to the ticket.

jon: Quick note — model-variant fallbacks should be part of the policy: prefer in-region quantized variants to avoid cross-region egress when possible. I'll sketch policy DSL examples.

tara: Also add telemetry keys we need in logs: tenant_id, routing_decision, fallback_reason, chosen_variant. Need those for audits.

maria: Good call. Final ask: keep messaging to customers simple: "Regional routing is designed to preserve data residency and reduce latency; in outage scenarios, we provide a documented fallback that may route requests to other regions unless you opt into strict residency (beta)." Approve?

sam: Approve.

jon: Approve.

tara: Approve.

ops-bot: reminder: sync scheduled Fri 11:00am PT, calendar invite in thread.
